## Proof

The associated Legendre function with the Condon–Shortley phase convention is defined by

$$P_n^{m}(x)=(-1)^{m}(1-x^{2})^{m/2}\,\frac{d^{m}}{dx^{m}}P_n(x),\qquad P_n(x)=\frac{1}{2^{n}n!}\frac{d^{n}}{dx^{n}}(x^{2}-1)^{n}.$$

Setting $m=46$ and noting that $(-1)^{46}=1$ and $(1-x^{2})^{46/2}=(1-x^{2})^{23}$, we obtain

$$\boxed{\,P_n^{46}(x)=(1-x^{2})^{23}\,\frac{d^{46}}{dx^{46}}P_n(x)\,}.$$

Substituting the Rodrigues formula for $P_n(x)$ and combining the derivatives,

$$P_n^{46}(x)=\frac{(1-x^{2})^{23}}{2^{n}\,n!}\,\frac{d^{\,n+46}}{dx^{\,n+46}}(x^{2}-1)^{n}.$$

This is well-defined precisely when $n+46\le 2n$, i.e. $n\ge 46$, matching the stated assumption.

### Explicit series form

Using the expansion

$$P_n(x)=\frac{1}{2^{n}}\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}(-1)^{k}\binom{n}{k}\binom{2n-2k}{n}x^{n-2k},$$

the 46th derivative annihilates every term with $n-2k<46$ and otherwise gives

$$\frac{d^{46}}{dx^{46}}x^{n-2k}=\frac{(n-2k)!}{(n-2k-46)!}\,x^{n-2k-46}.$$

Since $\binom{2n-2k}{n}\frac{(n-2k)!}{(n-2k-46)!}=\frac{(2n-2k)!}{n!\,(n-2k-46)!}$, the surviving terms ($k\le\lfloor(n-46)/2\rfloor$) yield

$$\boxed{\,P_n^{46}(x)=\frac{(1-x^{2})^{23}}{2^{n}\,n!}\sum_{k=0}^{\lfloor (n-46)/2\rfloor}(-1)^{k}\binom{n}{k}\frac{(2n-2k)!}{(n-2k-46)!}\,x^{\,n-2k-46}\,}.$$

### Verification of consistency

- **Degree.** $P_n(x)$ has degree $n$; the 46th derivative has degree $n-46$; multiplying by $(1-x^{2})^{23}$ (degree $46$) gives total degree $(n-46)+46=n$. ✓
- **Parity.** $P_n(-x)=(-1)^{n}P_n(x)$, so $\frac{d^{46}}{dx^{46}}P_n(-x)=(-1)^{n}(-1)^{46}\frac{d^{46}}{dx^{46}}P_n(x)=(-1)^{n}\frac{d^{46}}{dx^{46}}P_n(x)$, and $(1-x^{2})^{23}$ is even, hence $P_n^{46}(-x)=(-1)^{n}P_n^{46}(x)$. ✓
- **Sign.** The Condon–Shortley factor $(-1)^{46}=+1$, so no overall sign appears. ✓
- **Existence.** $(x^{2}-1)^{n}$ has degree $2n$; the $(n+46)$-th derivative is non-zero iff $n+46\le 2n$, i.e. $n\ge 46$. ✓

Both boxed expressions are equivalent general forms of $P_n^{46}(x)$ valid for all integers $n\ge 46$.
